Tennessee

3 directory entries · Research in progress

  • Cherokee↗Historical homeland connection
    Connection & source
    Historical homeland connection

    Nation FAQ identifies southern Tennessee as part of earlier homelands; partial-state connection.

    Centuries before removal; source updated August 2026. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Chiaha↗Historical town connection in specialist reference
    Connection & source
    Historical town connection in specialist reference

    Dye places the fortified town of Chiaha on Zimmerman’s Island in the French Broad River near modern Dandridge, Tennessee, in the account of the 1540 expedition. The map record indexes that historical town connection.

    Sixteenth-century Chiaha town visited in 1540. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Chickasaw↗Historical homeland connection
    Connection & source
    Historical homeland connection

    Nation history explicitly names Mississippi, Kentucky, Alabama and Tennessee; broad regional connection, not statewide boundaries.

    Before nineteenth-century removal; broad history passage. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

These are starting lists, not a complete census. Modern borders help you navigate; they are not Indigenous homeland boundaries. A connection may be historical or present-day and does not imply presence throughout a region. Directory names can overlap; the profiles explain their relationships.
